summary: Coordinator SIGTERM grace period is fully consumed by unit wind-down in hard_stop_with

evidence.rationale: The variable `signalled_at` captures `Instant::now()` at the coordinator SIGTERM (line 346), but `wind_down_units` (line 356) consumes up to the full `grace.units` (12 s) before `wind_down_coordinator` is called; the deadline `signalled_at + grace.coordinator` is thus already expired or nearly expired when the coordinator wait begins.

report.title: Coordinator SIGTERM grace period is fully consumed by unit wind-down in hard_stop_with
report.attack_vector: Not Applicable — internal scheduling logic triggered by operator invoking `rupu agentiflow stop --now`.
report.description: In `hard_stop_with` (lines 326–374), the coordinator process group is SIGTERMed at line 345 and the absolute deadline for `wind_down_coordinator` is computed as `signalled_at + grace.coordinator` (line 358), where `signalled_at = Instant::now()` is captured immediately after the SIGTERM at line 346. However, between capturing `signalled_at` and calling `wind_down_coordinator`, the code calls `wind_down_units(run_dir, grace.units)` at line 356, which blocks for up to `DRAIN_TERM_GRACE` = 12 seconds (the full unit grace period). By the time `wind_down_coordinator` is invoked at line 358, the real-time elapsed since `signalled_at` may already equal or exceed `grace.coordinator` (also 12 seconds by default), leaving the coordinator deadline already in the past. `wind_down_coordinator` then immediately calls `pid_is_running` and, finding the process still alive, sends SIGKILL — depriving the coordinator of any time to complete its OAuth credential-write drain (up to 10 s + 750 ms), which is the explicit purpose of the 12-second grace.
report.impact: A coordinator that is still draining a rotated OAuth credential when `hard_stop` is called will be SIGKILLed before it can write the credential to disk, causing the next `rupu` invocation to require a fresh interactive login. This is the exact failure mode the grace period exists to prevent, as documented in the `DRAIN_TERM_GRACE` constant comment.

location.input: `rupu agentiflow stop --now` operator command, which calls `hard_stop` → `hard_stop_with`.
location.output: Coordinator process group receives SIGKILL with effectively zero grace, potentially before the credential write completes.

report.root_cause: The variable `signalled_at` captures `Instant::now()` at the coordinator SIGTERM (line 346), but `wind_down_units` (line 356) consumes up to the full `grace.units` (12 s) before `wind_down_coordinator` is called; the deadline `signalled_at + grace.coordinator` is thus already expired or nearly expired when the coordinator wait begins.

call_chain.passes_because: detached coordinator leads its own group

evidence.claim: signalled_at is captured immediately after SIGTERM at line 346
wind_down_units is called before wind_down_coordinator and can block up to DRAIN_TERM_GRACE (12 s)
DRAIN_TERM_GRACE and grace.coordinator are both 12 s by default, so the deadline is already consumed
The module doc states coordinator grace is 'counted from its own SIGTERM'
evidence.excerpt:
/// For the coordinator's own process group, when it leads one, counted from
/// its SIGTERM (the same default, for the same reason).

recommended_patch.notes: The original design intended `grace.coordinator` to be counted from the coordinator's SIGTERM. This can be preserved by subtracting elapsed time (`signalled_at.elapsed()`) from `grace.coordinator` with a floor of zero, but giving the full fresh grace after unit wind-down is simpler and equally safe since the coordinator's credential drain needs a known minimum window.

ci_cd_detection.body: Add a unit test in `reaper.rs` that calls `hard_stop_with` with `grace.units = Duration::from_millis(500)` and `grace.coordinator = Duration::from_millis(100)`, using a coordinator process that ignores SIGTERM for 200 ms. Assert that the coordinator is NOT SIGKILLed before at least 100 ms after `wind_down_units` returns.
ci_cd_detection.expect: Without the fix, the coordinator is killed immediately (0 ms grace left); with the fix, it lives for ≥ 100 ms after unit wind-down.

regression_test.body: Spawn a coordinator process that traps SIGTERM and sleeps 200 ms before exiting. Call `hard_stop_with` with `grace.units = Duration::from_millis(500)` and `grace.coordinator = Duration::from_millis(300)`. Record whether the coordinator exited naturally (200 ms) or was SIGKILLed.
regression_test.expect_vulnerable: The coordinator is SIGKILLed (it does not exit naturally within 200 ms of SIGTERM) because 500 ms of unit grace consumed the 300 ms coordinator deadline.
regression_test.expect_patched: The coordinator exits naturally (by its own SIGTERM handler) within 200 ms, and is not SIGKILLed.

replication_steps: Build rupu with the existing code.
While the coordinator is alive, invoke `rupu agentiflow stop --now`.

Observe via process tracing (e.g. strace -e signal) that SIGKILL is delivered to the coordinator group within milliseconds of `wind_down_units` completing, regardless of the configured 12-second coordinator grace.
report.references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution Using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization. See also: POSIX `kill(2)`, `DRAIN_TERM_GRACE` comment (reaper.rs:68–82), HardStopGrace::coordinator doc (reaper.rs:93–96).

summary: Stale broadcast cursor left after failed spawn causes missed broadcasts on retry dispatch

evidence.rationale: The broadcast cursor registration at line 65 executes unconditionally before `launcher.spawn` at line 73; a spawn failure returns early via `?` without removing the already-written cursor, leaving it permanently positioned at the failure-time tip.

report.title: Stale broadcast cursor left after failed spawn causes missed broadcasts on retry dispatch
report.attack_vector: Not Applicable — internal scheduling path triggered by the lead calling the `dispatch` tool.
report.description: In `FleetSupervisor::dispatch` (lines 57–84), the unit's broadcast mailbox cursor is registered via `Mailbox::read_broadcast` at line 65, **before** `launcher.spawn` is called at line 73. If `spawn` fails (returns `Err`), the cursor is permanently written to the mailbox store for a participant name that has no corresponding unit. On a subsequent retry dispatch with the same participant name (e.g. `recon#1`), the cursor is already positioned at the tip from the first, failed attempt. Any broadcasts sent between the failed dispatch and the successful retry are delivered from the wrong offset, causing them to be silently skipped and never delivered to the unit.
report.impact: A unit dispatched after a previously-failed dispatch of the same participant name will miss all broadcasts sent between the failed and successful dispatch. In multi-round fleet runs where a dispatch is retried (transient spawn error), the unit silently misses steering messages or board directives, producing incorrect behaviour.

location.input: Lead calls `dispatch` tool with any agent name; the spawning launcher encounters a transient or permanent error.
location.output: Stale broadcast cursor persisted in mailbox store; subsequent same-name dispatch inherits the wrong cursor position and misses intervening broadcasts.

report.root_cause: The broadcast cursor registration at line 65 executes unconditionally before `launcher.spawn` at line 73; a spawn failure returns early via `?` without removing the already-written cursor, leaving it permanently positioned at the failure-time tip.

call_chain.label: Mailbox::read_broadcast registers broadcast cursor
call_chain.passes_because: cursor registration is always attempted before spawn

call_chain.label: launcher.spawn fails
call_chain.passes_because: the agent exe is missing or any spawn-time error occurs

evidence.claim: Cursor is registered before spawn; on spawn failure the cursor is not cleaned up
A successful retry with the same participant name inherits the stale cursor
evidence.excerpt:
// F-BCAST-REGISTER: a unit must see broadcasts sent between its spawn
// and its first turn, but not the backlog from before it existed.

report.remediation: Move the `Mailbox::read_broadcast` call to after `launcher.spawn` succeeds, so no cursor is registered for a participant that has no corresponding unit.

recommended_patch.notes: Moving registration after spawn preserves the original intent (unit sees broadcasts from the moment it exists, not backlog) while eliminating the stale-cursor-on-failure defect.

ci_cd_detection.body: Add a test that: (1) dispatches with a launcher that always fails; (2) verifies the mailbox has a stale cursor for the participant; (3) dispatches again with a succeeding launcher; (4) sends a broadcast before the retry and asserts the unit receives it.
ci_cd_detection.expect: Without the fix, the unit misses the broadcast due to the stale cursor. With the fix, the broadcast is delivered.

regression_test.body:
1. Create a FailOnce launcher that fails the first spawn, succeeds the second.
2. Dispatch recon#1; assert Err.
3. Send a broadcast message.
4. Dispatch recon#1 again (succeeds).
5. Read the unit's broadcast messages and assert the step-3 broadcast is present.
regression_test.expect_vulnerable: The broadcast is silently missed because the stale cursor points past it.
regression_test.expect_patched: The broadcast sent between failed and successful dispatch is delivered to the unit.

replication_steps: Call `FleetSupervisor::dispatch` with a launcher that returns `Err(UnitError::Spawn(...))`.
Confirm that `Mailbox::new(run_dir).read_broadcast(participant)` has created a cursor entry.
Call `dispatch` again for the same participant with a succeeding launcher.
Send a broadcast between step 1 and step 3.
Observe via `Mailbox::read_broadcast(participant)` that the broadcast is absent from the unit's message stream.

summary: PID recycling window between pid_is_running check and kill_group in SIGKILL escalation loop

evidence.rationale: The `pid_is_running(pgid)` check at line 410 and the `kill_group(pgid)` call at line 412 are not atomic; the OS can recycle the pgid between the two calls, and there is no mechanism (such as `kill(pgid, 0)` returning ESRCH before kill, or signalling via a retained file descriptor) to make this atomic on POSIX.

report.title: PID recycling window between pid_is_running check and kill_group in SIGKILL escalation loop
report.attack_vector: Not Applicable — internal process-management logic invoked by the orphan reaper or operator hard-stop.
report.description:
In `wind_down_units` (lines 380–417), after the SIGTERM grace-period loop ends, the code iterates over `signalled` pgids and at line 410 calls `pid_is_running(pgid)` to decide whether to escalate to SIGKILL. Between that check returning `true` and the `kill_group(pgid)` call at line 412, the group leader can exit (its SIGTERM drain finishes), the OS recycles the pgid, and an unrelated new process group inherits it. `kill_group` then sends SIGKILL to the unrelated group. This is a classic check-time/use-time (TOCTOU) race on a process identifier.

The same race exists for the parallel check-and-kill in `wind_down_coordinator` (lines 428–435), though the `GRACE_POLL` sleep keeps the window narrow.
report.impact: If a pgid is recycled between `pid_is_running` and `kill_group`, an unrelated process group (spawned by any other program on the system) receives SIGKILL. On a busy system with many short-lived processes this is a low-probability but non-zero risk. In a containerised environment where pid namespaces limit recycling the risk is lower, but the code provides no guarantee.

location.input: Units SIGTERMed by the orphan reaper or `hard_stop`, which outlive their grace period.
location.output: SIGKILL delivered to an unrelated process group that inherited the recycled pgid.

report.root_cause: The `pid_is_running(pgid)` check at line 410 and the `kill_group(pgid)` call at line 412 are not atomic; the OS can recycle the pgid between the two calls, and there is no mechanism (such as `kill(pgid, 0)` returning ESRCH before kill, or signalling via a retained file descriptor) to make this atomic on POSIX.

call_chain.gate: Instant::now() >= deadline or no signalled pgid is alive
call_chain.passes_because: at least one pgid was still alive at the last poll

call_chain.label: pid_is_running(pgid) — true
call_chain.passes_because: group leader still present at this instant

call_chain.label: OS recycles pgid (race window)
call_chain.gate: group leader exits, pgid assigned to new unrelated group
call_chain.passes_because: POSIX allows pid reuse with no lock

call_chain.label: kill_group(pgid) sends SIGKILL to wrong group

evidence.claim: pid_is_running check and kill_group are separate, non-atomic operations with no lock between them
GRACE_POLL is 25 ms — short enough that a dying process can exit and its pgid be recycled between the check and the kill on a loaded system
The module doc itself acknowledges pgid recycling as a concern for the pre-SIGTERM guard, but not for the post-grace SIGKILL path
evidence.excerpt:
// Only a group whose leader is still there: a fully dead group's number
// may have been recycled onto something that is not ours.

report.remediation:
There is no fully portable atomic check-and-kill on POSIX. The best practical mitigations are:
1. **Accept `ESRCH` from `kill`** — if `kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` returns `ESRCH`, the group is gone and the pgid may be recycled; log and skip rather than treating it as an error. This is already what `kill_group` should do for a dead group, so verify it handles `ESRCH` correctly.
2. **Narrow the window** — eliminate the `pid_is_running` pre-check before `kill_group`; instead, call `kill_group` unconditionally and interpret the return value. If the group is already dead, `kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` returns `ESRCH`, which is safe to ignore. This removes the TOCTOU window entirely at the cost of occasionally sending SIGKILL to an already-dead group (harmless).
3. **Document the residual risk** in the safety comment, as the pre-SIGTERM guard already does for the same class of problem.

recommended_patch.notes: Removing the `pid_is_running` guard means SIGKILL is sent unconditionally to every pgid that was SIGTERMed and did not finish within the grace. If the group is already dead, `kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` returns `ESRCH`, which `kill_group` should already handle. The log level is lowered to `debug` since a dead group at SIGKILL time is not an error.

ci_cd_detection.body: Add a Clippy/lint rule or a code review checklist item: any `pid_is_running(p)` followed by `kill*(p, ...)` within the same block without an intervening atomic mechanism must be flagged. Additionally, a sanitiser-assisted test (using a fast-recycling PID namespace) can be run nightly.
ci_cd_detection.expect: A nightly test that rapidly forks/exits processes detects the double-send or unintended-recipient kill within 100 iterations.

regression_test.body: Write a test that: (1) spawns a process group that SIGTERMs but delays exit for 10 ms; (2) calls wind_down_units with a 1 ms grace; (3) records what pgids received SIGKILL. After patching, confirm that kill_group is called exactly once per pgid and that an ESRCH return is treated as non-fatal rather than as an error log.
regression_test.expect_vulnerable: pid_is_running check passes, then process exits, then kill_group is called on the now-recycled pgid (observable in high-concurrency or PID-namespace tests).
regression_test.expect_patched: kill_group is called unconditionally; ESRCH is logged at debug level and the function returns without error, regardless of whether the group is still alive.

replication_steps: Run the orphan reaper or `hard_stop` on a system under high process churn (many short-lived processes constantly recycling pids).
Observe via audit log or eBPF that `kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` is occasionally delivered to a pgid whose leader is a newly-spawned unrelated process.
The probability scales with system load and the duration of the SIGTERM grace period.

cross_references.note: Both findings are in the reaper/hard-stop process-management path and relate to timing correctness of signal delivery.

report.references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution Using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization. POSIX `kill(2)` manual: ESRCH returned when no process or process group can be found matching pid. Linux `pid_namespaces(7)`: PID recycling behaviour. See also the pre-SIGTERM pgid-recycling guard comment at reaper.rs:387–389.
